questions.text: The bridge seems like the obvious approach, which is exactly why the opposing captain avoids it. questions.text: Several banners have appeared beyond the wall, creating the impression that the defenders are preparing to advance. questions.text: The commander has rejected two proposals that would have preserved her forces: waiting for additional supplies and circling through the northern woods. Both options would delay the encounter, allowing our engineers to finish the central defenses. Her remaining decision is therefore consistent with a rapid frontal commitment, despite the risk of exposing the group on open ground.
questions.zh: 指挥官拒绝了等补给和绕北林两种保全兵力的方案，因为两者都会拖延，让我方工兵完成中央防御。因此剩下的决策指向快速正面投入，尽管全队有暴露于开阔地的风险。

stories.text: When Mara arrived, she asked for neither a bed nor a meal. She wanted a pencil. Before leaving, she placed the map beside the door. "A useful map tells people what they need," she said, "not just what is there." We have kept a pencil beside it ever since.

stories.title: 第一顿共同的晚饭
stories.text: We have only one large pot, but six people want to cook. At first, everyone talks at once. Then we choose one simple dish. Two people cut vegetables, two bring water, and the others make a fire. Dinner is late, but nobody eats alone.
stories.zh: 大家一开始争论菜谱，后来选择人人都能参与的一道菜。共同完成比选出最完美的菜更重要。

stories.title: 第一顿共同的晚饭
stories.text: The first shared dinner nearly failed before anyone lit the fire. Six people had six recipes and only one pot. Arguing about the best dish took longer than preparing it would have. Finally, Jin suggested that they choose a meal everyone could help make. It was not anyone's favorite, but it gave each person a useful task. By the time they sat down, the food was almost beside the point: the strangers had learned how to work together.

stories.title: 会休息的菜园
stories.text: The garden looks empty today. We picked the last vegetables yesterday. Our neighbor says the soil needs time to rest. We cover it with leaves instead of planting again at once. An empty field can still be part of a good plan.
stories.zh: 收获后给土壤休养的时间。暂时空着并不等于计划失败。

stories.title: 会休息的菜园
stories.text: After the harvest, I wanted to plant every empty patch immediately. A garden full of green leaves seemed more successful than bare soil. Our neighbor disagreed. She explained that the previous crop had used many of the nutrients that the next one would need. We covered part of the ground with fallen leaves and left it alone. For a while, progress looked like doing less. The following season helped me understand why waiting had been part of the work.

stories.title: 走慢一点的快路
stories.text: There are two roads to the village. The short road has deep mud. The longer one is dry. We choose the dry road and arrive before the other cart. Distance is not the only thing that makes a journey long.
stories.zh: 雨后捷径泥泞，较长的干路反而更快。判断不能只看地图距离。
stories.prompt: 较长的路为什么更快？
stories.explain: 雨后捷径泥泞，较长的干路反而更快。判断不能只看地图距离。

stories.title: 走慢一点的快路
stories.text: The driver was embarrassed to choose the longer road. On the map, it looked like an unnecessary detour, and the other travelers laughed when he turned away from the shortcut. But the recent rain had changed the calculation. While the first cart struggled through deep mud, ours kept moving at a steady pace. We reached the village with daylight to spare. The experience reminded us that the shortest route on paper is not always the quickest route in practice.

stories.title: 一次没被嘲笑的错误
stories.text: I use the wrong English word when I ask for a bowl. My friend looks confused, then shows me the word I need. We laugh together. Later, I use it again without help. The mistake becomes a small part of a real conversation.
stories.zh: 说错单词后，朋友用实物帮助理解。真实语境中的再次使用，让词更容易被想起。

stories.title: 一次没被嘲笑的错误
stories.text: I had practiced the sentence in my head, yet the wrong word came out when I finally spoke. For a moment, I considered pretending that I had meant something else. My friend simply picked up a bowl and said its name. There was no test to fail and no score to lose. Later that evening, I needed the same word again. This time it arrived more easily. What I remembered was not a rule on a page, but the moment when someone understood me.

stories.title: 借来的工具
stories.text: Our hammer breaks, so we borrow one from the next camp. We return it the following day. A week later, they ask for our saw. Soon we build a small shelf for shared tools. We do not need to own everything ourselves.
stories.zh: 邻里借工具逐渐发展为共享制度，付出一些协调成本，换来更丰富的可用工具。
stories.prompt: 共享工具的主要好处是什么？
options: 能使用各家不必单独买齐的工具
stories.explain: 邻里借工具逐渐发展为共享制度，付出一些协调成本，换来更丰富的可用工具。

stories.title: 借来的工具
stories.text: At first, every household planned to buy a complete set of tools. The cost was high, and most tools would have remained unused for weeks. A broken hammer led to a different arrangement. After borrowing a replacement, we began keeping a list of what each neighbor could share. There were occasional delays, and someone had to maintain the list, but the system gave everyone access to more equipment than they could have afforded alone.
stories.zh: 邻里借工具逐渐发展为共享制度，付出一些协调成本，换来更丰富的可用工具。

stories.title: 没有数字的进步
stories.text: Last month, I could not read the notice at the gate. Today, I understand most of it. There is no prize, and nobody is watching. I still stop for a moment and smile. Something that once blocked my way has become useful.
stories.zh: 真正的变化是原本难懂的告示现在能读懂大意，不一定需要外部奖品来证明。

stories.title: 没有数字的进步
stories.text: The notice had been on the gate for weeks. On my first visit, its long sentences had looked like a wall of unfamiliar shapes. I took a photograph and forgot about it. When I returned, I could follow the main message without opening a dictionary. I still missed two details, but the difference was real. No level appeared above my head. The reward was that a piece of the world had become easier to understand.

stories.title: 雨天的来信
stories.text: A letter arrives after three days of rain. Our friend cannot visit this week because the river is too high. She sends a story instead. We read it together by the fire. The visit is delayed, but the friendship is not.
stories.zh: 河水过高使拜访延期，朋友寄来故事，让联系得以继续。

stories.title: 雨天的来信
stories.text: We had prepared an extra bed before the rain began. Three days later, a messenger arrived with a letter explaining that the river was no longer safe to cross. Our friend apologized for changing the plan and included a story from her own village. We read it aloud after dinner. The empty bed still reminded us of the visit we had expected, but the letter gave us something different to share. A postponed plan did not have to become a lost connection.
stories.zh: 河水过高使拜访延期，朋友寄来故事，让联系得以继续。

stories.title: 修好的旧门
stories.text: The hall has a new roof and new windows. We keep the old front door. It is not perfect, but many visitors wrote their names on it. The building is better now, and it still remembers the people who helped us begin.
stories.zh: 旧门留着建设者的名字。修补而保留它，是效率与记忆之间的取舍。

stories.title: 修好的旧门
stories.text: During the repairs, someone suggested replacing the old front door. A new one would fit the frame more neatly and keep out a little more wind. Yet the old wood carried the names of nearly everyone who had helped establish the camp. We repaired its weakest parts and kept it. The decision was a small compromise between efficiency and memory. Improving a place did not require removing every sign of the work that had made it possible.
stories.zh: 旧门留着建设者的名字。修补而保留它，是效率与记忆之间的取舍。

stories.title: 一次只改一个地方
stories.text: Our bread is too hard. We change the flour, the water, and the cooking time. The next loaf is better, but we do not know why. After that, we change only one thing each time. Learning becomes slower to start and easier to trust.
stories.zh: 同时改许多因素会难以判断原因，一次改变一个因素更便于获得可靠经验。

stories.title: 一次只改一个地方
stories.text: The first successful loaf caused an argument. One cook credited the new flour, another the extra water, and a third the shorter baking time. Because we had changed everything at once, none of us had convincing evidence. For the next few attempts, we kept careful notes and changed one part of the recipe at a time. This approach felt less exciting than trying a completely new recipe, but it gave us knowledge that could be used again.

stories.text: The roof is repaired. There is food for dinner and wood for the fire. We could keep working, but we choose to stop. Tomorrow has its own tasks. Tonight, we sit outside and enjoy the place we have made.

stories.title: 够用的一天

Those observations were true, but they did not make the day incomplete. We had finished what we set out to do. Instead of opening another project immediately, we carried our chairs into the yard. For once, the camp was not a list of future improvements. It was a place where we could live.

stories.title: 第一辆经过的商车
stories.text: The bridge is ready. A cart crosses it slowly, carrying books, cloth, and tea. The driver stops to thank us. Until today, the bridge was our project. Now it is part of someone else's journey. We watch the cart disappear down the road.
stories.zh: 第一辆商车通过后，桥从建设任务变成真正帮助他人的道路。工程完成，价值开始兑现。

stories.title: 第一辆经过的商车
stories.text: We had spent so much time measuring, carrying, and repairing that the bridge had become a collection of tasks in our minds. Then the first cart arrived. Its driver knew nothing about the arguments over the design or the afternoon when a wheel had broken. He simply crossed the river, stopped to thank us, and continued toward the next village. Watching him leave changed the meaning of the work. The bridge was finished, and its usefulness had only just begun.
